# XSE conformance fixtures

Each scenario writes zero-byte files into its own temporary root. No installed game, registry, or user settings are required. Detection absence maps to null (the pack was authored when the Node and CXX surfaces exposed an absence sentinel rather than distinct errors); no error-category coverage is claimed. Exact byte inventory verifies observation did not add, remove, or modify fixture files.

The optional `kind` selects F4SE, F4SEVR, SKSE, SKSE64, SKSEVR, or SFSE; omitted `kind` preserves the original F4SE fixtures. Every variant has missing, loader-only, and detected scenarios with a variant-owned loader and `1_10_163.dll` filename.

The contract was corrected in place (the shared Rust semantic runner accepts only family version 1; the changed expectations still change the pack's expectation digest): the XSE version is read from the loader's embedded PE version resource, never from a sibling runtime DLL's filename (that filename names the game runtime the build targets, not the script extender's version). The `*-detected` scenarios keep their stable IDs and now pin that regression: a zero-byte loader carries no version resource, so the version stays null even though a `<prefix>1_10_163.dll` sits beside it. A zero-byte fixture cannot carry a resource, so the conversion from the PE file version to the XSE version is covered by unit tests in `classic-xse-core` instead.
